source_documents.title: Oxidation-state-controlled switching between AIE and ACQ in pyrene luminophores

reference_evidence_units.quote: The flexible sulphide exhibits weak emission, partial conformational locking in the sulfoxide enables strong AIE through suppression of nonradiative decay, whereas the rigid sulfone undergoes aggregationcaused quenching (ACQ).
reference_evidence_units.subject: DS, DSO, DSO2
reference_evidence_units.statement: Oxidation state switches between weak emission, AIE and ACQ.

reference_evidence_units.quote: These results reveal that AIE arises from a delicate interplay between conformational restriction and excitedstate nature, extending beyond conventional restriction of intramolecular rotation mechanisms.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DS, DSO, DSO2
reference_evidence_units.statement: AIE depends on both conformational restriction and excited-state character.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Despite similar emission energies, the quantum yields (FF) increase from DS (0.13) and DSO (0.23) to DSO2 (0.53), indicating suppression of non-radiative decay in the fully oxidized system (Table S1).
reference_evidence_units.subject: DS, DSO, DSO2

reference_evidence_units.quote: Consistently, DSO2 displays the most pronounced red-shift, indicative of strengthened intramolecular charge transfer (ICT) arising from enhanced donor–acceptor character.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DSO2
reference_evidence_units.statement: The sulfone has the strongest ICT character.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The flexible and packing-sensitive DS system undergoes only modest emission enhancement due to persistent non-radiative pathways, whereas the partially rigidified DSO achieves an optimal balance between conformational restriction and excited-state stabilization, leading to pronounced AIE.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DS vs DSO
reference_evidence_units.statement: Flexible DS keeps nonradiative channels; partly locked DSO shows strong AIE.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Upon oxidation, conformational freedom is progressively reduced, enforcing an orthogonal orientation of the phenyl ring relative to the pyrene core (Fig. 4d and e).
reference_evidence_units.subject: DSO, DSO2
reference_evidence_units.statement: Oxidation locks the tolyl rings orthogonal to pyrene.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Notably, the enhanced PLQY of DSg originates primarily from suppression of the knr, while the kr rates remain comparatively similar across the polymorphs.
reference_evidence_units.subject: DS polymorphs
reference_evidence_units.statement: The brightest DS polymorph differs by knr, not kr.

reference_evidence_units.quote: leading to a highly rigid and electronically decoupled arrangement (Fig. 5c)
reference_evidence_units.subject: DSO2

reference_evidence_units.quote: adopts a highly rigid and tightly packed structure that promotes non-radiative deactivation, resulting in aggregation-caused quenching
reference_evidence_units.subject: DSO2
reference_evidence_units.statement: Tight packing quenches the sulfone in the solid.
reference_evidence_units.limitations: No intermolecular electronic coupling identified (packing called decoupled).

reference_mechanisms.label: RIM_RIR_RIV
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Strong AIE through partial conformational locking (orthogonal tolyl rings) that suppresses nonradiative decay.

reference_mechanisms.rationale: The paper adds excited-state stabilisation from oxidation as the second ingredient of the AIE.

contrast_group.varied_factor: oxidation state of the two sulphur linkers (sulphide vs sulfoxide)
contrast_group.paper_difference: The flexible sulphide shows only modest aggregation enhancement; the sulfoxide, with tolyl rings locked orthogonal, shows strong AIE.

basis: m-CPBA oxidation product of DS (main text, SI)
